gaps.concept: The LH surge completes meiosis I; the ovulated cell is a secondary oocyte arrested in metaphase II.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks which meiotic division occurs immediately before ovulation.

gaps.concept: Primary oocytes are diploid with replicated DNA (2n, 4C); secondary oocytes are haploid with replicated DNA (1n, 2C).
gaps.why_tested: A meiosis diagram asks for chromosome number or DNA content at ovulation.

gaps.concept: Oogonia enter meiosis during fetal life; most follicles undergo atresia, leaving a finite ovarian reserve.
gaps.why_tested: An age-related fertility stem asks why the supply of oocytes declines.

gaps.concept: Primordial germ cells originate near the yolk sac and migrate to the developing gonadal ridge.
gaps.why_tested: An embryology stem asks where ovarian germ cells originated.

gaps.concept: Primordial follicles have flattened follicular cells; primary follicles acquire cuboidal granulosa cells and a zona pellucida; antral follicles develop a fluid-filled cavity.
gaps.why_tested: An ovarian micrograph asks the learner to identify the follicle stage.

gaps.concept: Theca interna is vascular and steroidogenic; theca externa is fibrous, while granulosa cells lie inside an avascular basement membrane.
gaps.why_tested: A histology image asks which follicular layer produces steroid precursors.

gaps.concept: Follicles and corpora lutea occupy the ovarian cortex; large vessels and nerves occupy the medulla.
gaps.why_tested: An ovarian section asks the learner to identify its cortical and medullary regions.

gaps.concept: Falling FSH selects one dominant follicle with high FSH sensitivity; competing follicles undergo atresia.
gaps.why_tested: A cycle stem asks why one follicle usually reaches ovulation.

gaps.concept: Pulsatile hypothalamic GnRH stimulates anterior pituitary FSH and LH release; continuous GnRH exposure suppresses gonadotropins.
gaps.why_tested: A hormone-tracing or drug stem asks why continuous GnRH agonist exposure prevents ovulation.

gaps.concept: Estradiol usually inhibits gonadotropin release; sustained high estradiol switches feedback to positive, producing a large LH surge and smaller FSH surge.
gaps.why_tested: A cycle graph asks why gonadotropins remain low before their midcycle peaks.

gaps.concept: Estradiol peaks before ovulation and rises again modestly during the luteal phase; progesterone peaks in the mid-luteal phase.
gaps.why_tested: An unlabeled menstrual-cycle graph asks the learner to identify hormone curves.

gaps.concept: The corpus luteum secretes progesterone, estradiol, and inhibin A; inhibin A suppresses FSH during the luteal phase.
gaps.why_tested: A luteal-phase hormone pattern asks which ovarian structure and inhibin isoform are responsible.

gaps.concept: Without implantation, corpus luteum regression lowers progesterone and estradiol, releasing FSH from inhibition to recruit the next follicular cohort.
gaps.why_tested: A cycle graph asks why FSH begins rising around menstruation.

gaps.concept: Embryonic hCG acts at LH receptors to preserve the corpus luteum and progesterone production in early pregnancy.
gaps.why_tested: An early-pregnancy stem asks why menstruation does not occur before placental progesterone production is established.

gaps.concept: Menstruation sheds the endometrial functionalis; the basalis remains and regenerates the lining during the proliferative phase.
gaps.why_tested: A uterine histology stem asks which layer is lost or retained during menses.

gaps.concept: Progesterone withdrawal increases prostaglandins and spiral-artery constriction, causing endometrial ischemia and menstrual cramps.
gaps.why_tested: A dysmenorrhea stem asks for the mediator of uterine contractions and pain.

gaps.concept: Anovulatory cycles lack a corpus luteum and luteal progesterone; persistent estrogen stimulation causes irregular shedding without secretory endometrium.
gaps.why_tested: An irregular-bleeding stem pairs a hormone pattern with endometrial histology.

gaps.concept: Fertilization normally occurs in the fallopian tube ampulla.
gaps.why_tested: An anatomy stem asks where the ovulated oocyte usually meets sperm.

gaps.concept: A corpus luteum cyst may hemorrhage or rupture, causing sudden unilateral pelvic pain after ovulation.
gaps.why_tested: An acute-pain stem asks the learner to distinguish a luteal cyst from a follicular cyst.

gaps.concept: Clomiphene blocks hypothalamic estrogen feedback, increasing FSH and LH to induce ovulation.
gaps.why_tested: An infertility drug stem asks how an estrogen receptor modulator stimulates follicular development.

gaps.concept: Letrozole inhibits aromatase, lowering estrogen feedback and increasing FSH to induce ovulation.
gaps.why_tested: An infertility drug stem asks how aromatase inhibition promotes ovulation.

gaps.concept: Combined hormonal contraceptives suppress the gonadotropin surge and ovulation through estrogen and progestin negative feedback.
gaps.why_tested: A contraception stem asks how exogenous hormones prevent oocyte release.
